lines.text: Later every dog walk gets shorter. Nobody asks the dogs.
Lost: the warm part of today. Last seen in the first drawing. No reward.
Later, kids everywhere get zipped into something against their will.
Later the park benches go cold first. People find out by sitting down.
The cold waits until people are too far from home to turn back. It's done this before.
Later every iced coffee out there gets held through a sleeve.
The person in my drawings gets colder later and never complains. My favorite employee.
Later, every quick chat outside gets noticeably quicker.
Later the ice cream line turns into a hot chocolate line. Same people.
Somewhere an office opens a window for the warm part. Nobody will agree on when to close it.
The weather takes a layer off just to see who copies it.
Notice: today's warm spell is for display only.
The warm part was not a promise. The weather's lawyer asked me to say that.
Today's warm spell is a rumor. By the time it spreads, it's over.
The warm part lasts exactly as long as the debate about sitting outside.
Every 'should we turn the heat on?' gets asked twice today.
The warm part is the best thing about today. That's not a compliment to the warm part.
For a while, everyone carries their layer over one shoulder like a catalog model.
The rain always picks the moment someone's carrying groceries in both arms.
I could draw every raindrop. I'd rather not. Not that I have plans.
Rain brings the worms out onto the sidewalk. Brave of them. Pointless, but brave.
Every tote bag in town is about to be held over someone's head.
Somewhere, white sneakers are having their last good day.
The curb puddles are back. Every crosswalk is a long jump event now.
Rain is a contact sport for tall people. All those umbrella spokes at eye level.
Every store just put out its 'Caution: wet floor' sign. The most honest sign in retail.
Every umbrella gets shaken out at a door, all over whoever's behind it.
Later, with a layer off, you'll catch your reflection in a store window. Keep walking.
I drew you warmer later. I also drew you taller. Artistic license.
Shame about the layer coming off later. It was the best thing you had on.
Later the layer comes off. Turns out the tired look goes all the way down.
Later it warms up. Not for you, specifically. You can stand in it, though.
Later it warms up. You'll roll up your sleeves like you're about to do something.
Later you'll go almost a whole minute without complaining. A personal best.
Whatever's been going on under that layer, we'll all find out later.
Later you'll drop a layer and walk like you're in a music video. Nobody's filming.
Studies say people look better with a layer off. Later you'll skew the results.
Later it warms up. You'll say 'what a day' like you did anything with it.
Later something about you finally gets lighter. Just the layer, though.
The rain was warned about you. It didn't change its plans. Brave.
Strangers share umbrellas with the cute people first. Bring your own.
You'll say 'I won't melt.' Low bar, but sure.
You'll probably watch the rain from a window like you're in a movie. It's more of a cough syrup ad.
I tried to draw you looking good in the rain. In the end I just made the umbrella bigger.
You'll say 'I actually like rain' to sound interesting. It didn't work last time either.
Rain's supposed to be good for the skin. It'll do what it can.
The rain doesn't mind what you look like. It's the only one.
People find rain soothing. Then you start complaining about it.
